finding.claim: The /rss endpoint passes the user-supplied `u` query parameter straight to URI.open. The server fetches any URL the caller names, including internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF. On Ruby versions before 3.0, open-uri's Kernel#open behavior could also open local files, but URI.open itself only handles URLs.

trace.note: params[:u] is passed unvalidated to URI.open, which performs the HTTP(S)/FTP request
first 400 bytes of the response body are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, or IP allowlist or denylist. No private-range or metadata-address blocking. No redirect restrictions. TRUSTED is defined but not used on this route.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes params[:u] directly to URI.open(...).read with no validation, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes. TRUSTED (app.rb:5) is only checked on /trusted (app.rb:14), not on /rss.
